items.title: The depth of a Cohen-Macaulay module against an ideal as a difference of dimensions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file dualizing.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement computes the depth of a finite Cohen-Macaulay module with respect to a nontrivial ideal as the difference between the dimension of its support and the dimension of the support of the quotient by the ideal (author lemma at source lines 2060-2067, label lemma-depth-CM). The proof (source lines 2069-2091) runs an induction on the depth: in the zero case the ideal sits inside an associated prime which then supports the quotient, and Cohen-Macaulayness upgrades the resulting inequality to an equality; in the induction step a nonzerodivisor in the ideal is divided out, and both the depth and the dimension of the support drop by exactly one, which keeps the identity in step (proof lines 2083-2090). The induction and the base case are the substance. H3.
